decisions.statement: A wait ends early where the service has been asked to stop.
A wait is where a service that keeps running leaves for code that moved.
The tick before a wait has landed, which is what makes the wait a safe point.
A service leaves as a wait opens rather than as a wait ends.
A wait a service defers its first tick by is waited out, so that deferral is never lost.
A stop already asked is answered before code that moved is weighed.
A wait says whether that wait ran out or was ended early.
A loop reads that answer to know whether to stop.
A wait asked for after the stop was asked returns at once.
SIGTERM and SIGINT both ask a service that keeps running to stop.
A timer left behind holds the process up.
Every wait clears its own timer.
No service that keeps running writes this wait for itself.

definition: the wait between one tick of a service that keeps running and the next
